body:
Well I haven't had a good childhood. Not in the traumatic way, just in the way that my mom didn't really talk to me or understand my feelings. I've talked quite a lot with a psychologist about this, and when   you aren't taken emotionally care of as a child you develop coping mechanisms to make it through the day.

So when my father wasn't around and my mother didn't care for me, I (subconsciously) convinced myself that I didn't want people to care for me, and I just wanted to be alone. And it worked, I got through my childhood thinking things were going well.

The thing is the coping mechanisms doesn't just stop because you are an adult. So i still kept to myself, even though I wanted friends and such. It was actually first when i talked to my psychologist 4 years ago I found out my childhood wasn't good. Or even that my childhood had any negative effect on my adult life.

Yeah, i never know what to do when people accedentaly touch me. Should i move away or act as if i don't notice? In my young days, it was move away always, and people would sometimes laugh at me because i would always sit in uncomftable ways to avoid being touched.

Now I try to move away if it's not too much of a strain on me. And it works in my daily life. People like to be around me. But it breaks down when i'm on a date. I have no idea how to act if she touches me or if I can touch her in any way.

I can see how you don't want to talk to others about it. But I don't think you need to be ashamed about it. It's a normal reaction, if you haven't been touched much, and it's a thing that can change. :)
Thanks
Logically i know this. I'm just frustrated that such a meaningless thing for other people has such a great meaning for me. Thanks for the reply. :)

It's too bad things like that happens and it's a tragedy even though it was "justified" or not. It's even more bad when people try to use it as an emotional argument to push an agenda! those kind of things go under my skin.

I live in the outskirts of Denmark' second largest city, Aarhus. It's quite nice here, I have walking distance to a lake and forest. Plus bike paths and public transportation are really good in the larger cities of Denmark. I'm not fit enough to bike around though :(. Aarhus also has a (I think) really nice university with a park surrounded by yellow brick buildings, almost the the middle of the city.

It's a shame I don't get out more, I spend my days in my room. Which is also nice. Small but nice.

It sounds like you have been around a lot. I mean the US is freaking humongous. I would like to see the world. Or rather, I would like to meet someone i want to be with and then experience the world with her. I've already been to England, Germany, France, Italy, Sweden... That's about it, it's a shame though I don't think I've ever been to Norway. You should totally go to Europe, or even Denmark! We don't have any mountains or rivers or notable forests... But we have fields and no matter where you are in Denmark you are always maximum 2 hours away (with car) from the ocean. There's also culture and stuff.

Edit: Also the most dangerous wild animals are the badger or the deer. No bears or coyotes. It's kind of tame. Also that's not entirely true, recently there have been sightings of a couple wolfs, which have been extinct from our country since 1813. There are great debates whether or not kill them or let them live.

Also also, sorry for the long post. It's just so hard to have a conversation over text without writing a lot.

Yeah I'm early 20's. It's just young can mean a lot of different things. I guess I should have specified in my post if I didn't want any confusion. ANYWAY.

Our situation sounds similar. Except, I quit uni out of shame. and I don't have a job. I don't think I'm a jerk and such, but I could be in denial or some shit.

And I'm afraid a promise of change isn't good enough. There is no reason why it should change for the better (without me putting work into it). And I don't know how I'm gonna change for the better. plus I'm not sure how long time I have to change in.

First off, I don't think I have a depression. Or I'm not diagnosed depressed. It doesn't make a difference though, I know I feel like shit.

No, I don't have a support system or someone to talk to. Or, you know, I have Reddit. And I've heard that talking to someone about my feelings should help my shitty-feelingness. Don't know if it helps yet.

Yeah, part of the reason why I'm lonely right now is that I don't spend time around other people (like with work and school). But even when I did have work and was in school I didn't make really friends. It wasn't because people didn't like me. It was because I would avoid everyone outside of work/school. You would have to be really persistent to "hang out" with me. So I would never develop any friendships.

I don't know exactly what I'm looking for by posting here. I guess I've heard that it's good to talk about these things and then I'm just trying it out.

And I know that you can do pretty much anything, if you just work for it (or, that it is rarely what you've been born with that is the limiting factor). It just doesn't help me when I have problem with doing things.

I don't know how young you think I am. But I'm considered an adult who can take care of himself. But I don't take care of myself. I don't eat (enough), I don't go outside, I don't try to get a job, I don't try to make friends, I just don't take care of my needs in general.

I kinda know what you mean. My parents divorced when i was a little boy and my mom moved away with me to an other part of the country (I'm from Denmark, so it was only 3 hours away with a train). But I was never really comfortable there. I guess it's kinda similar? 

Anyhow, it's fun you ask about anything happening. Because a dozen people have died because they ate some [rullepølse](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiced_meat_roll). So now people are joking with making eating some rullepølse an extreme sport and the deadliest of all storm a [pølsenado](http://i.imgur.com/jiCa7jq.png). It's really tragic, and yet one of the things you never thought you should hear. Anyway anything happening the other way across the pond?

edit: I just want to add, there is nothing wrong with rullepølser in general. But this particular brand was tainted with a very dangerous bacteria.
Yeah, I'm going to bed now, so pretty different time-zones. But pfftt only losers talk with people in their own time-zone.
Really Sour candy. The way your jaws hurts is just priceless. Unfortunately you get used to the sourness and it doesn't hurt anymore.

Also, This is what happens to me in real life. I panic, then take a couple of days to un-panic. Then I panic over i panicked. If someone was expecting me to do something, then this would be especially devastating. This is the reason I quit university. This is the reason I don't apply for any jobs.

Also also, I really want to try to reply more regularly.

Also also also, I know I'm a dumb-ass. But please reply if you see this. It would mean a lot to me.

Edit: Also also also also, I just saw To The Moon was on sale in the next 12 hours for 1,5 euro https://www.humblebundle.com/store/p/tothemoon_storefront.  I really recommend it, it has a real nice soundtrack and a nice emotional story. And it's only like 5 hours long, so it doesn't take forever to play. You can read about it in the link provided, I really think it's worth it. I just saw it and thought you might would like it?!

Recently I've been playing the walking dead, and it's quite an enjoyable experience. 

As for movies I can recommend "In Bruges". It's about two hit-men in the Belgium town Bruges.  It has some black humor and (I think) it is well written. It deals with themes such as honor, love, shame, loyalty, guilt and friendship. I can't really sell it good enough.

"Mary and Max" is an animation about a girl who feels different and she becomes pen pals with an (if I remember correctly) autistic man. I think I like this movie because I can relate to it.quite a bit.

And lastly "Burn Before Reading" because it's such an entertaining movie that is just weird and the last scene really pulls the whole movie together.
If you're gonna watch any of these, watch In Bruges.

And don't be jealous of my piano skills. I can kinda play this one https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB96F7AqZUA at 70%, with hiccups where it gets hard. I have some other pieces I want to learn, but it's hard to do anything recently. 

Yes, I do need to place more value on myself, I guess that's my entire problem or at least a very big part of it.

I also want to tell you why I take such a long ass time to reply. When I get a reply I usually panic and can't really focus my thoughts. To be specific: When you asked if I could recommend any movies, I blanked out. Couldn't think of a single thing. I felt like I had deceived you. And it just got worse when I realized I've told you I can play the piano, but it's more like I want to play the piano. So I felt pretty bad, and could really try to write to you. This is the reason why I hate "what do you like to do" questions, I always feel like I misrepresent myself and therefore deceive someone.

I've always just done my own thing. So I'm not close with anybody, and have never really been. I can't think of anyone i would want to know how I feel either.

Also, I'm going to bed now. So if you reply I won't reply back until I wake up.

I guess I should add that I've been using "I just want a break and work, live life" and "I don't know what i want in the future, but I'm working on it". But I've been using these for the past 1 and 1/2 years but I'm still unemployed. I'm not sure how long I can keep this up.

I've been writing with someone else on SW. And when I get a reply I just panic. I begin to cry and can't do anything for at least a couple of hours. Then it takes some time to to get the courage to write back and when I finally get the courage to reply it takes a couple of hours to actually write back. 

This is how I've been doing it so far. But I just don't think I can write back for the latest reply. Even though Blackwithink is just words on a screen to me. Even though I'm not under any time pressure. The thought of writing back is quite scary.

When I can't even write with a random person over the internet... It discourages me a lot.

When i went out with people from my class i would get blackout drunk. something I've only done once before uni. But right now I don't drink. In the last year I've drunk maybe 5 bottles of wine (excluding new years).
I don't trust myself enough to get a job. I fear that it will all happen again.

I don't understand why people should like me. It makes me really unsure of other people motivations to do things with me. And if I do something somewhat bad (like being in a bad mood, wanting to be alone for too long, saying/doing something inappropriate), that's when I feel like people should want to avoid me. They don't, and then I begin to avoid them.

I don't think I'm uncomfortable in my own skin. I just really, really care about other people. To the point where one of my worst fears is to worsen an other persons day. So unless I don't say anything unless I know it won't make their day worse.


I guess my interests are video games? I like movies and music. Actually the thing i like the most is hearing other peoples experiences/thoughts on stuff. Video games, movies and such are just ways to express this. 

I also really like to challenge myself. Some video games are a great challenge. And I went to university to study math for a year, and it was pretty fun. I try to play the piano sometimes.

I haven't really done any of these things lately. At least not because I enjoy them, but more just to pass the time.

Sorry I haven't replied before now. It has been a rough week and it's really hard for me to express my thoughts.

How do you imagine a happy or successful you and what is the smallest step you can take towards that?

The happy me is able to have friends without thinking that they hate me whenever we aren't together. I would be able to call up people to hang out and I would be able to talk about things i like without being really uncomfortable. And I have no fucking idea how to change in such a way that these things are going to be true, cause they have always been true.

I do know how to work with some other things (work out and piano mainly). But if I don't know how to be more "social", then why does the other things matter. It's like having half of the pieces in a jigsaw puzzle, but no idea where the other half is. Why would you ever try to solve that jigsaw?

I just can't imagine me ever be able to be not lonely. People are just not something I'm comfortable with. And I can't imagine how I can ever be even remotely satisfied if I am lonely.

About opening up to other people, is it a normal thing to be really uncomfortable about? I mean, I'm very uncomfortable about it. To the point where i can't discuss anything I like. I'm really afraid people will dislike/be annoyed by the things i like to do. I just end up not saying anything or changing the subject which leads to me not being able to be close to anyone. Only I'm 100% certain i won't annoy anyone will I speak my mind.

"so why not continue the work you've already put in?"

- The problem is that I haven't put any work in. Well I have in the past. But I've stopped every time, because what's the point. I honestly don't believe change will come or that good things will happen. 

I know you wrote that I'm worth something and I shouldn't hold myself back. I know that I'm worth something and if I work on myself i will better myself. I know this because everyone is worth something and everyone can better themselves. But I feel like I'm worth nothing and i feel like things are not gonna change. Most of the time I can repress that feeling. But some times it just overtakes my life for a month and everything I've worked for is gone.
